question: A new architect joins your extraction team before the system is connected to a downstream contract database. She asks why the design returns contract data through an extraction tool with a JSON schema instead of asking Claude to write JSON in its text reply. You must give her the reason that this design choice rests on. Which reason is accurate?

options.text: Tool use halves the cost of each extraction request compared with text replies, so the design saves money when the document volume is high.
options.reason: The guide gives the 50% cost savings to the Message Batches API, not to tool use; tool use is chosen for reliable schema-compliant output.

options.text: Tool use lets the team drop format normalization rules from the prompt, because the schema itself converts inconsistent dates and currency formats in the source documents into one standard form.
options.reason: The guide says to include format normalization rules in prompts alongside strict output schemas, because the schema alone does not handle inconsistent source formatting.

options.text: Tool use enforces the schema when tool_choice is set to "auto", because Claude then decides for each document whether structured output is needed.
options.reason: The guide states that with tool_choice "auto" the model may return text instead of calling a tool, so this setting does not enforce structured output.

options.text: Tool use with a JSON schema is the most reliable way to get schema-compliant output, because it eliminates JSON syntax errors in the extracted data.
options.reason: The guide names tool use with JSON schemas as the most reliable approach for guaranteed schema-compliant structured output, because it eliminates JSON syntax errors.
